title: Read halal labels with confidence
purpose: Educational prompts only. Ingredient names cannot independently prove a final product is halal.

reference.label: Jamaica Halal Council: Halal Food General Guide

ingredients.title: Gelatin / gelatine
ingredients.why: Gelatin can be derived from different animal sources, and a generic label may not establish which animal or processing method was used.
ingredients.ask: Which animal or alternative source was used, and is its certification valid for this formulation?
ingredients.note: Ask for species, supplier and processing evidence. Do not assume all gelatin has the same status.

ingredients.title: Animal fats, shortening & lard
ingredients.alsoKnownAs: rendered fat, animal shortening, pastry fat
ingredients.why: Animal fats can come from different species and processes. Pork-derived lard is not acceptable under the referenced halal guidance.
ingredients.ask: Is the fat plant-based or animal-derived? If animal-derived, what species and verified sourcing?
ingredients.note: Read the actual supplier declaration; do not treat generic ‘animal fat’ as a verified halal ingredient.

ingredients.title: Meat stock, extracts & broths
ingredients.alsoKnownAs: beef stock, chicken broth, meat flavour
ingredients.why: An animal's species name does not establish how the meat or its derivatives were obtained or handled.
ingredients.ask: Does the source meat have applicable halal verification, and are processing and shared equipment controlled?
ingredients.note: Check the actual meat supplier and certificate scope, not just the flavour description.

ingredients.title: Collagen
ingredients.why: Collagen often originates from animal tissue; the actual source matters for suitability.
ingredients.ask: Which species, supplier and processing route supplied this collagen?
ingredients.note: Products with the same ingredient name may have different sourcing histories.

ingredients.title: Rennet
ingredients.why: Rennet or related enzymes may be sourced from animals, microbes or other processes.
ingredients.ask: What is the enzyme's source and was the whole production chain assessed?
ingredients.note: The label ‘vegetarian cheese’ or ‘rennet’ alone does not document all halal criteria.

ingredients.title: Food processing enzymes
ingredients.why: Processing enzymes can originate from different organisms, culture media and handling methods.
ingredients.ask: What is the enzyme source and, where relevant, its fermentation medium and downstream process?
ingredients.note: A processing aid may not be obvious on a finished food's ingredient panel.

ingredients.title: Glycerin / glycerol
ingredients.why: Glycerol may be vegetable, synthetic or animal-derived; the label often does not disclose which.
ingredients.ask: Is the glycerol plant-based, synthetic or animal-derived, and what documentation supports it?
ingredients.note: Do not infer the origin solely from its additive or E-number.

ingredients.title: Mono- and diglycerides
ingredients.why: Certain food emulsifiers may be derived from vegetable oils or animal fats, depending on formulation.
ingredients.ask: Are the fatty acids vegetable or animal-derived, and is there supporting supplier evidence?
ingredients.note: E-numbers identify an additive class, not necessarily its biological source.

ingredients.title: Natural and artificial flavours
ingredients.why: Broad flavour descriptors do not reveal every carrier, extraction solvent, or processing aid.
ingredients.ask: Does the flavour use animal-derived inputs or alcohol-based carriers? What evidence covers the final product?
ingredients.note: A natural flavour is not automatically a verified halal flavour.

ingredients.title: Vanilla and other extracts
ingredients.why: An extract may involve solvents or processing conditions that matter to halal assessment.
ingredients.ask: Which solvents and extraction processes were used, and what does the relevant certifier say?
ingredients.note: Interpretation and accepted treatment can differ; consult a qualified authority for a ruling.

ingredients.title: Fermented foods & condiments
ingredients.why: Fermented foods vary in manufacture, ingredients and possible alcohol-related processing considerations.
ingredients.ask: What are the production ingredients and processing details, and is any halal assessment documented?
ingredients.note: Do not categorize an entire fermented-food group without product-specific evidence.

ingredients.title: Whey and processed dairy
ingredients.alsoKnownAs: whey powder, cheese powder, milk derivatives
ingredients.why: Milk-derived ingredients may also be connected with enzymes, additives and manufacturing aids.
ingredients.ask: Are rennet, enzymes and any processing aids documented for this specific supply chain?
ingredients.note: An ingredient may be dairy-based yet require further production checks.

ingredients.title: Halal marks & certificates
ingredients.alsoKnownAs: halal logo, certificate number, certifier seal
ingredients.why: A printed mark, especially on concept packaging, is not independent proof of a current certificate. Its issuer, validity, product/facility scope and authenticity matter.
ingredients.ask: Who issued the certificate, what does it cover, when does it expire, and can the issuer confirm it?
ingredients.note: Tayyib's own packaging concepts are not evidence of commercial certification.

ingredients.title: Shared equipment & cross-contact
ingredients.why: Ingredients alone may not reveal production, storage and transport practices that can affect halal suitability.
ingredients.ask: Were preparation equipment, storage and transport reviewed for the specific operation?
ingredients.note: Follow the whole documented process; do not rely solely on a front-of-pack logo.
